nodes.summary: Tree metrics satisfy the four-point condition (the easy direction of Buneman's theorem).
nodes.title: Tree metrics satisfy the four-point condition

nodes.summary: The four-point condition: `d x y + d z t ≤ max (d x z + d y t) (d x t + d y z)`.
nodes.title: Four-point condition

nodes.summary: A symmetric dissimilarity on a finite set that vanishes on the diagonal is a tree metric if and only if it satisfies the four-point condition.
nodes.title: Buneman's four-point theorem

nodes.summary: A symmetric dissimilarity on a finite set that vanishes on the diagonal and satisfies the four-point condition is a tree metric.
nodes.title: Buneman's theorem, converse direction

nodes.summary: `d` is a tree metric: there are a finite tree `G` on a vertex type `V`, positive edge lengths `w`, and a placement `ι` of the taxa on vertices such that `d x y` is the total length of the (unique) path from `ι x` to `ι y`.
nodes.title: Tree metric

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
